title: Steam build and redistributable readiness
excerpt: A PC release needs a reproducible depot build, required redistributables, clean-machine launch testing and rollback-ready build identification.
lesson: Build configuration and clean-machine smoke testing precede store release.

title: Steam Cloud integration
excerpt: Cloud storage requires explicit save paths, quotas and synchronization behavior across machines.
lesson: Local save schema and failure handling precede cloud sync and conflict tests.

title: Steam stats and achievements
excerpt: Persistent stats and achievements need stable identifiers, initialization, unlock conditions and offline synchronization behavior.
lesson: Progression events precede platform stat mapping and achievement QA.

title: Android device coverage
excerpt: Android launch planning covers hardware tiers, screen shapes, touch input, graphics, audio and representative physical-device tests.
lesson: Define a supported-device matrix before optimization and release QA.

title: Android stability and memory
excerpt: Release quality includes crash and ANR monitoring, memory behavior, frame consistency, startup time and background lifecycle tests.
lesson: Profiling and lifecycle QA are release tasks, not post-launch cleanup.

title: iOS TestFlight and submission
excerpt: Create the app record, upload a versioned build, complete metadata, distribute through TestFlight and resolve review findings before release.
lesson: Signing, metadata, beta testing and review buffer belong in the delivery schedule.

title: iOS build identity
excerpt: Uploaded builds are associated through bundle ID and version data and must finish processing before testing or review.
lesson: Bundle identity, signing and version automation precede upload and TestFlight QA.

title: Web game persistence
excerpt: Browser persistence must account for storage quotas, eviction, private browsing and asynchronous APIs.
lesson: Choose a storage and recovery strategy before promising durable saves or offline play.

title: Web game loading and performance
excerpt: Web delivery benefits from bounded initial downloads, compressed assets, progressive loading and profiling across browser and device classes.
lesson: Asset budgets and loading strategy precede content-scale commitments.

title: Web input and focus
excerpt: Browser games must handle keyboard, pointer and touch input alongside focus loss and browser-reserved interactions.
lesson: Input abstraction and focus-state tests precede control customization.
